data.long_meaning: The name Shahabaz is derived from Persian and Arabic origins. It is composed of two words: Shah, meaning king or lord, and Bahaz, meaning world. The name thus translates to 'Lord of the World' or 'Ruler of the Universe'.

data.cultural_impact: The name Shahabaz carries rich cultural connotations. Its Persian and Arabic origins highlight the historical influence of these ancient civilizations on India and its people. The name's grandeur and regal associations evoke images of powerful kings and rulers from Hindu mythology and history. Moreover, the name's diversity, combining elements of Persian and Arabic cultures, reflects the multicultural fabric of India.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Shahabaz represents the belief in a higher power ruling over the universe. It underscores the concept of divinity pervading all aspects of creation. The name may also be interpreted as a reminder of the individual's potential to rule their own inner worlds and, ultimately, achieve spiritual enlightenment. In Hinduism, where the pursuit of inner peace and self-realization holds great importance, the name Shahabaz could serve as a powerful inspiration and source of motivation on the spiritual path.

historical_references.reference: Shahabaz Khan was a notable Mughal commander and a close confidant of Emperor Shah Jahan. He was a Persian nobleman, and played a key role in the Battle of Samugarh in 1661, where the Mughal forces defeated the Maratha confederacy led by Shivaji Bhonsle.

Shahabaz Khan also served as the Subahdar (Governor) of Bengal during the reign of Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb in the late 17th century. During his tenure, he expanded the Mughal territories in Bengal and Bihar, and established the city of Murshidabad as the capital of Bengal Subah.
